question.value: Search for high-mass prestellar cores in the Orion GMC and resolve their internal structure.

evidence.quote: In this work, we set out to carry out a systematic search for high-mass prestellar cores in a single giant molecular cloud (GMC), the Orion GMC.
We then use ALMA to resolve these candidate HMPCs to investigate their internal structure.

referee_caveats_inferred: The N2D+ upper-limit prescription conflicts: the table note uses 3σ, while the prose uses SNR = 10 for both species.
The prose kinetic-temperature range of 30–140 K conflicts with the tabulated ORS-7 P1 value of 163 K.
Both bands are assigned a 28.6″ maximum recoverable scale in Observations, yet the size interpretation invokes a larger Band 6 recoverable scale.
The <11 M⊙ conclusion depends on adopting a 15 K lower temperature limit; the explicit 10 K calculation reaches 21.4 M⊙.
Warm gas and low deuteration support an evolutionary interpretation but do not directly establish an embedded protostar in every core.
Requiring detection in both bands imposes a selection effect that is not quantified.
A null result for seven selected sources does not by itself establish cloud-wide absence or distinguish nonexistence from a short lifetime.
Mass and size comparisons across instruments need consistent treatment of spatial filtering, angular resolution and temperature assumptions.
The integrated-line noise expression omits an explicit channel-width factor; its numerical implementation is unclear.
